Title: COBSTP Inauguration Speech
CentralBank: Central Bank of So Tom and Prncipe
text: Central Bank of S. Tome Principe 11/06/2005-DISCURSO DE S.E O VICE  GOVERNOR ON THE OCCASION OF THE INAUGURATION OF THE COMMERCIAL BANK STP (COBSTP) Your Excellency, President of the Republic Your Excellency, Mr President of the National Assembly Your Excellency, Prime Minister and Head of Government Your Excellency, Madam President of the Supreme Court Your Excellency, Mr President of the Court of Auditors Your Excellency, Members of the Government, Your Excellency, Distinguished Guests Excellencies Ladies and gentlemen, let me, in brief words, make use of the opportunity offered to us by the inaugural occasion, which marks the institutionalization and entry of the "Commercial Bank STP" into our market, to allude to a date, which is immemorably and without which, it would be unthinkable and above all expendable our presence in this honorable event. It is thirty years ago tomorrow that the people of S.Tome and Principe have achieved their political independence and accepted the mtiplos challenges that then came to an unpunished, towards the ecological development, which obviously includes the development of the national financial system. Many generations of men and women who have done better in this struggle have not seen July 12, 1975, nor have they lived long enough to witness the reform and growth of the national financial system. Is in memia of these men, who, I would like to ask for your indulgence, so that we may hold a minute's silence. THANK YOU VERY MUCH! Excellencies Ladies and gentlemen, I wanted the fate that our short existence would allow us to witness profound changes in the national ecological and financial fabric. Changes have not always been fruitful, as good intentions have not always sufficed. It turns out, however, that the financial system in particular and the economy in general are too sensitive to social upheavals; so much more commitment and much more determination is needed in what we do. Because it is histia, what we do today and it is built, without haste, with surrender and much selflessness. It occurs to me to remind you that the banking, in the last century, provided relevant service to the country, making with its tender a great contribution to the consolidation and internationalization of large agricultural companies in STP, financing projects that allowed this territory to reach in 1913 the brand of the largest producer of cocoa in 1913. Then we had a mostly illiterate population, with few means and plausible sobs; but, they were original in their time and earned respect and admiration. The fmulas of banking in the past were simple and consisted of making the government its ally, the national business partner and the national economy a point of arrival and not a starting point. Excellencies Ladies and gentlemen, to Dr Yves Michel Fotso, Chairman of the Board of Directors of The Commercial Bank STP, to whom we express our consideration and appreciation, we would like to greet you and through you to the entire board of directors of your Bank and to tell you that, in fact, what we expect from Banca is originality, creativity and compliance with the law; santomense economy is a virgin and promising economy. Therefore, it is with the rise honor that we invite you to receive the certification that testifies to the institutionalization of The Bank-STP Commercial in the financial square of S.Tome and Principe ... Despite the efforts already made in these last thirty years and ongoing structural reforms, we still have important and several challenges such as: - Overcoming technological and knowledge delays; -Development of indispensable eco-and social infrastructure -Urbanization, land planning and environmental balance. -Adoption of a market-oriented development strategy, where the improvement of the competitiveness of the Santomense economy and its dynamic insertion in the regional and global economy, constitute the dominant strategy of the main axes of econic policy in the prime times. It should be noted that at the level of the financial system there is also much to be done: - There is to develop the Payment Means System supported by the advanced information technologies available; - The interbank money market must be implemented as a preliminary phase of a future capital market. Our vision of the future suggests that we challenge econic and financial operators to face the possibility of turning S.Tome and Principe into an international financial square, and therefore preparing to the ambitious goal. To this end, it is unavoidable to enhance our comparative advantages in the necessary competitive advantages on a global scale. On the other hand, STP must prepare to take advantage of the opportunities offered to us by the Free Movement of Goods Agreement, signed with the Econica Community of Central African States, and the US initiative (AGOA), among others. These premises of stp development require that innovative financial capital mobilization are found, through the establishment of a partnership between the plico sector and the private sector, national and foreign, naturally presupposing the transition from a development model based on plicos investments to a model based on competitiveness, and in this context, the financial system is called upon to play a key role. And it is also in this context that we welcome the entry into our market of the "Commercial Bank STP", because it is another financial intermediary that puts itself at the service of ecooperators and the economy in general, producing added value and generating jobs; An example of how south south cooperation is working in our country. Therefore, we expect from the most newcomer of our partners, a dynamic and aggressive attitude, that meets the business, that supports him and proposes effective, sustained and innovative options and exits, making this his strategic ally. Finally, I would like, on behalf of the Central Bank of STP, and in my opinion, to reiterate our thanks to the promoters of the commercial Bank STP for their commitment to the Santomenses economy and financial system and to cast votes for success in your activity. Welcome to all and thank you very much for your attention. Made in S. Tome, on 11 July 2005 Deputy Governor DR. EUGeNIO LOURENcO SOARES

Title: Economic Balance Sheet 2005
CentralBank: Central Bank of So Tom and Prncipe
text: Econmic Balance of the Year 2005 Summary of the lecture given by Mr. Governor of BCSTP ECONOMIC PERFORMANCE 2005 The year 2005 was marked by an unfavorable international economic conjuncture, mainly translated by: Increase in the Price of Petrleo Successive increases in the interest rate of the EDF Appreciation of the Dlar Decrease in the Price of Cocoa and Natural Disasters, among others This situation negatively influenced the level of macro-economic performance, having a direct impact on the deterioration of the exchange term, worsening of the level of inflation with consequent loss of purchasing power and decrease in external donations. Nevertheless, several budgetary constraints have been imposed on us, resulting from external commitments and our relationship with the Bretton Wood organisations, with a view to reaching the point of completion within the framework of the Enhanced HIPC initiative, with a view to the forgiveness of our external debt. These restrictions have made us somewhat apprehensive as their impact on the reduction of public investment was indeed significant. In the internal context, there were several constraints that also contributed to the current performance of the national economy to be highlighted: Political instability, with repercussions on the level of investments, both external and internal; Prolonged drought with impact on the decrease in cocoa exports, Successive disruptions of commodity stocks; Loss of purchasing power as a result of the impact of rising fuel prices on national and international markets. In view of the constraints, the economic year was still satisfactory, since the current economic performance (GDP of 3.8%) led to the country's approval in the evaluation test in September last with the IMF and WB, opening the door to the forgiveness of external debt under the HIPC initiative. The implementation of this plan will bring significant improvements to the standard of living of our population, with a direct impact on poverty reduction. OUTLOOK FOR 2006 We are open to good prospects for the economic year 2006, as, in addition to the difficulties that are still mltiplas, a rigorous and prudent management, with the competition and sacrifice of all Santomense citizens, has gained international recognition and led to the round table held in Brussels foreshadowing improvements in the external environment with regard to donations. In this context, GDP growth is projected to be around 4.5%, higher than in the last three years, and inflation well below that recorded in the year ended (less than 13%). Drilling of the first oil block in January 2006 will certainly produce a multiplier effect resulting from improved levels of confidence in the economy with increased investment and employment. Another element of trust and likely to boost tourism is strengthening the privileged relationship that STP has with cplp countries, Nigeria, Taiwan and the USA. As far as the Central Bank is in question, we will continue to make efforts to improve the supervision of the financial sector in order to ensure the operationality of this sector. In this sense, it is essential for the year 2006 to connect to swift's international networks, establishments of agreements with the international networks of cards (Master Card, Visa), as well as the completion of the feasibility analysis of an interbank network of ATMs. With regard to the private sector, we warn of better management of available resources in order to direct them to the creation of long-term jobs and not only short-term, as demonstrated by the credit structure for this sector, where construction takes a significant part of the total credit granted. Central Bank of Sao Tome and Principe December 2005

Title: Economic Balance Sheet 2007
CentralBank: Central Bank of So Tom and Prncipe
text: Econico Balance Sheet of the year 2007 Speech given by the Deputy Governor of BCSTP Excellencies Ladies and gentlemen, First, I would like to address the cordial greetings to all those who follow us at this time and, as has already been a tradition, I must present the balance sheet of the year 2007. In a context of very unfavorable international economic conjuncture, the national economy has now revealed moderate economic growth between 4 and 6%, despite the persistent deterioration in the consumer price index that is estimated to reach 24.3%. The construction, tourism and other services sectors, supported by public and private investments, have contributed to this economic growth, which is more driven by domestic demand. It should be noted that the aforementioned economic growth did not count on the contribution of the exporting sector of goods, such as cocoa which decreased in the period, despite the increase in its price on the international market. The importance of domestic demand in the contribution to economic growth is confirmed by the increase in credit to the private sector by 27%, reaching a level of 549 thousand folds in November of this year, against 431,000 million the previous year. The sectors that benefited from this increase were construction, trade and industry with a share of 35, 22 and 21.8 % respectively. The current developments reveal a slowdown in the pace of creation of the secondary currency which in the previous year had reached 47%, points to an attempt to adjust and contain domestic demand due to high interest rates; however, not reflected in the decrease in the consumer price index. In the monetary sector, there was an increase in the monetary base of 45% at the same time as the monetary mass indicators, M2 and M3 grew by 24% and 40%, respectively. In contrast, net credit to the government reached -171,000 million doubles against -108 million doubles the previous year. Reasons for concern is the high rate of defaults on credit repayments in the financial system as a whole, which is 33%, i.e. 143,000 million doubles of loans overdue and not honored by borrowers, and the high rate of foreign currency credit (45%). The external sector proved very listless, with the balance of the trade balance and current account increasingly untainable, a scenario that translates into a sharp deterioration in import coverage by export. This evolution of the external sector, by maintaining, is compromising the efforts of managing external reserves, which are encrypted in 4 months of import, which, despite being in line with international recommendations, should not be accommodated by the current trends of variation of the current balance of payments account, as this would greatly hinder the macro-economic objectives of combating imbalances in the context of exchange and monetary policies. The depreciation of the national currency by about 21% against the euro and 9.8% against the dlar demonstrates the pressure that the two currencies (double and dlar) have suffered in the face of the rise of the euro in the international market. The maintenance of inflationary pressure, despite the high interest rate and high level of minimum cash reserve, shows a weakness in monetary and fiscal restraint policy, as well as the indirect control mechanisms currently underway, while demonstrating to us that it is difficult to maintain a pace of economic-based growth, almost exclusively, in internal demand. It is therefore urgent to encourage the exporting sector of goods, goods, services, in order to effectively combat the chronic external imbalance as an integral part of the macroeconomic consolidation. We must not lose sight of the risks of external shocks to which the national economy is subject, which makes it potentially and delicately vulnerable, and therefore demanding permanent and courageous structuring measures until the fundamental macro-economic imbalances are eradicated. As we said at the beginning, the international economic situation is not favourable to non-oil exporting countries, as is the case with S.Tome and Principe. Reinforcing this unfavorable situation we have the escalation of the price of this fuel in the international market that approached 100 dollars per barrel against the 63 dollars in 2006, associated with the appreciation of the euro against the dlar by 10%, further aggravated by the prospects of slowing the pace of economic growth worldwide, following the real estate crisis in the United States of America. Your Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen, It is for this reason that the process of consolidation and relaunch of the national economy will require increasing effort of cross-sectoral coordination, greater discipline and greater rigor in management. OUTLOOK FOR 2008 The economic outlook for 2008 is favourable, taking into account the that the country will begin to benefit from the fact that it has managed to reach the point of completion of the enhanced HIPC initiative. In this context, GDP growth for 2008 is projected to be 6% and inflation between 9 and 12%. The prospect of donations from the Millennium Challenge Corporation, the World Bank, the ADB and Brazil, among other development partners, could result in an important multiplier, associated with improved levels of confidence in the national economy. In this context, the Central Bank will, among others, trigger the following actions: -Implement, in partnership with other competent authorities, the interbank money market to strengthen monetary policy and help banking, today with more operators, to better diversify its financial packages, thus creating a first platform of financial instruments traded on an open market; -Continue the effort, together with financial operators, to modernize the payment system based on high Information Technology; -Continue to make efforts to improve the supervision of the financial sector; -Progressively adapt preventive supervisory mechanisms prudential rules and capital adequacy requirements for basel's successive regulations; -Introduce new account plans to the financial system as better respond to the new requirements in the classification of financial activities. -Relaunch the studies on the monetary integration hipsters of S.Tome and Principe so that, as the Issuing Bank and economic advisor to the government, the Central Bank can have a technical and formal position on the issue. In this study, the decision of the 31st ordinary meeting of the governors of African central banks together with the African Union to relaunch a joint action plan to create an African Central Bank, including a single currency, on the continent's scale should be taken into account. AT THE END, I WOULD LIKE, IN MY OWN NAME, IN THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS AND IN THE WORKERS OF THE CENTRAL BANK, TO WISH THE FINANCIAL OPERATORS IN PARTICULAR, TO THE ECONOMIC AGENTS AND TO THE GENERAL PUBLIC HAPPY PARTIES AND A PROSPEROUS NEW YEAR'S DAY. THANK YOU SO MUCH. DECEMBER 2007

No sector monet<87>rio registou-se, nesse per<92>odo, um aumento da base monet<87>ria de 45% ao mesmo tempo que os indicadores da massa monet<87>ria, M2 e M3 cresceram em 24% e 40%, respectivamente. Em contrapartida o cr<8e>dito l<92>quido ao governo atingiu -171 mil milhes de dobras contra os -108 mil milhes de dobras do ano anterior. Motivos de preocupa<8d><8b>o constitui o elevado <92>ndice de incumprimentos nos reembolsos de cr<8e>ditos, no conjunto de sistema financeiro, que se situa em 33%, ou seja, 143 mil milhes de dobras de empr<8e>stimos vencidos e n<8b>o honrados pelos mutu<87>rios, sendo tamb<8e>m de destacar a elevada taxa de cr<8e>dito em moeda estrangeira (45%). O sector externo revelou-se muito ap<87>tico, com os saldos da balan<8d>a comercial e da conta corrente cada vez mais inst<87>veis, cen<87>rio que se traduz numa acentuada deteriora<8d><8b>o da cobertura de importa<8d><8b>o por exporta<8d><8b>o. Essa evolu<8d><8b>o do sector externo, ao manter-se, <8e> comprometedora dos esfor<8d>os de gest<8b>o de reservas externas, cifradas em 4 meses de importa<8d><8b>o, que apesar de estarem em linha com as recomenda<8d>es internacionais, n<8b>o devem se acomodar <88>s actuais tend<90>ncias de varia<8d><8b>o da conta corrente de balan<8d>a de pagamentos, j<87> que isso dificultaria, sobremaneira, os objectivos macroeconmicos de combate a desequil<92>brios no <89>mbito de politicas cambial e monet<87>ria. A deprecia<8d><8b>o da moeda nacional em cerca 21% frente ao euro e 9,8% frente ao dlar demonstra a press<8b>o que as duas moedas (dobra e dlar) sofreram face a subida do euro no mercado internacional. A manuten<8d><8b>o da press<8b>o inflacionista, n<8b>o obstante a alta taxa de juro e alto n<92>vel de reserva m<92>nima de caixa, revela uma notria fragilidade na pol<92>tica de conten<8d><8b>o monet<87>ria e fiscal, bem como dos mecanismos de controlo indirecto actualmente em curso, ao mesmo tempo que nos demonstra que <8e> dificilmente sustent<87>vel manter um ritmo de crescimento econmico baseado, quase exclusivamente, na procura interna. Urge-se, por essa raz<8b>o, incentivar o sector exportador quer de bens, quer de servi<8d>os, para se combater, eficazmente, o crnico desequil<92>brio externo enquanto parte integrante do pacote de consolida<8d><8b>o macroeconmica. N<8b>o podemos perder de vista os riscos de choques externos a que est<87> sujeita a economia nacional, o que a torna potencial e delicadamente vulner<87>vel, e por isso, exigente de medidas de estrutura<8d><8b>o permanentes e corajosas, at<8e> que sejam erradicados os fundamentais desequil<92>brios macroeconmicos. Tal como o dissemos ao princ<92>pio, a conjuntura econmica internacional n<8b>o se revela favor<87>vel aos pa<92>ses n<8b>o exportadores de petrleo como <8e>, ainda, o caso de S.Tom<8e> e Pr<92>ncipe. A refor<8d>ar essa desfavor<87>vel conjuntura temos a escalada do pre<8d>o desse combust<92>vel no mercado internacional que se aproximou dos 100 dlares por barril contra os 63 dlares de 2006, associada a valoriza<8d><8b>o do euro face ao dlar em 10%, agravada ainda mais, pelas perspectivas de abrandamento do ritmo de crescimento econmico mundial, na sequ<90>ncia da crise imobili<87>ria nos Estados Unidos de Am<8e>rica. Excel<90>ncias, Meus Senhores e minhas Senhoras, <83> por essa raz<8b>o que o processo de consolida<8d><8b>o e relan<8d>amento da economia nacional exigir<87> cada vez maior esfor<8d>o de coordena<8d><8b>o intersectorial, maior disciplina e maior rigor na gest<8b>o. PERSPECTIVA PARA 2008 A perspectiva econmica para 2008 afigura-se favor<87>vel, tendo em conta que o pa<92>s come<8d>ar<87> a beneficiar do facto de ter conseguido atingir o ponto de conclus<8b>o da iniciativa HIPC refor<8d>ada. Neste contexto projecta-se um crescimento do PIB para 2008 de 6% e uma infla<8d><8b>o entre 9 e 12%. A perspectiva de entrada de donativos do Millennium Challenge Corporation, do Banco Mundial, do BAD e do Brasil, entre outros parceiros de desenvolvimento, poder<87> resultar num importante multiplicador, associado a melhorias de n<92>veis de confian<8d>a na economia nacional. Neste <89>mbito ser<8b>o desencadeadas, por parte do Banco Central, entre outras, as seguintes ac<8d>es: -Implementar, em parceria com outras autoridades competentes, o mercado monet<87>rio interbanc<87>rio para fortalecer a politica monet<87>ria e ajudar a banca, hoje com mais operadores, a melhor diversificar seus pacotes financeiros, criando assim uma primeira plataforma de instrumentos financeiros negociados em regime de mercado aberto; -Prosseguir o esfor<8d>o, em conjunto com os operadores financeiros, de moderniza<8d><8b>o do sistema de pagamento baseada na alta Tecnologia de Informa<8d><8b>o; -Continuar a envidar esfor<8d>os no sentido de melhorar a supervis<8b>o do sector financeiro; -Adequar, progressivamente, os mecanismos de supervis<8b>o preventiva <88>s exig<90>ncias de regras prudenciais e de adequa<8d><8b>o de capitais <88>s sucessivas normativas de Basileia; -Introduzir novos planos de contas para o sistema financeiro como forma de melhor responder <88>s novas exig<90>ncias na classifica<8d><8b>o das actividades financeiras. -Relan<8d>ar os estudos sobre as hipteses de integra<8d><8b>o monet<87>ria de S.Tom<8e> e Pr<92>ncipe por forma que, na qualidade do Banco Emissor e de assessor econmico do governo, Banco Central possa ter uma posi<8d><8b>o t<8e>cnica e formal sobre a quest<8b>o. Nesse estudo a decis<8b>o da 31<bb> reuni<8b>o ordin<87>ria dos governadores dos bancos centrais africananos conjuntamente com a Uni<8b>o Africana, de relan<8d>ar um plano de ac<8d><8b>o conjunto para criar, a escala do continente, um Banco Central Africano, incluindo uma moeda nica, dever<87> ser tomada em conta. AO TERMINAR, GOSTARIA, EM MEU NOME PR<ee>PRIO, NO DE CONSELHO DE ADMINISTRA<82><cc>O E NO DOS TRABALHADORES DO BANCO CENTRAL, DESEJAR AOS OPERADORES FINANCEIROS EM ESPECIAL, AOS AGENTES ECON<ee>MICOS E AO P<f2>BLICO EM GERAL FESTAS FELIZES E UM PR<ee>SPERO ANO NOVO. text: Econmic Balance of the Year 2008 Speech given by Mr. Governor of BCSTP Excellencies Ladies and gentlemen, Firstly, on behalf of myself and the Members of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of St. Thomas and Principe, I would like to thank you all at this traditional end-of-year meeting in which we take stock of the year that is about to end and present the prospects for the first year. We started 2008 in an adverse international situation, mainly due to the volatility of the petreo price, which reached the maximum of more than 150 Dares per barrel by mid-September 2008, against about 100 Dares of the year 2007. Fortunately, the signs that come to us at this end of the year feed us a certain optimism in this area, especially in the impact on cereal and petreo price levels, and this thymus is reaching values below 40 a barrel, but which contrasts with the financial crisis that currently affects the world. The current unstable international financial situation, due to the financial crisis that has increased and spread rapidly in this great quarter, has been observed by the Central Bank with some concern, and we are extremely concerned about its possible negative impact on the various spheres of national life, mainly in the economic and social spheres. S. Tome is Prince cannot therefore remain indifferent to this unfavourable international situation over which we have no control. Ladies and gentlemen, We are a small economy, inserted in the international market, dependent on the outside, not of import to meet much of our basic needs in food, energy and equipment, as well as in the financing plan the economy in general. Despite the very unfavorable international context, the Santomense economy proved to be, in the year that now ends, a moderate economic activity with GDP growing between 5 and 6%, that is, the same as in 2007. The construction sectors, associated with tourism, communications, trade, financial services, among other services, have contributed to this performance of GDP growth, which continued to be the main determinants of growth, adding to the momentum given by foreign direct investments. Despite this good performance of the GDP behavior of the previous years, the level of economic activity of the country is still little expressive and manifestly insufficient to enhance development and social well-being. It should be noted that cocoa exports have increased slightly as a result of their price increase on the world market, however, the contribution of the agricultural sector to economic growth remains rather weak. Ladies and gentlemen, A stable and competitive financial system can contribute decisively to economic growth and the necessary macro-economic stability, as it is of fundamental importance in supporting such key factors as investment, development, modernisation and innovation; conditions which, as we all know, are inseparable from the growth of our economy, currently living in an environment of globalisation. The importance of demand for credits is an example of how the financial system can enhance development, and this is justified by the increase in credit the economy, reaching a level of 639,000 million folds in the current year, against 619,000 million folds in the previous year. The sectors that benefited the most from this increase were construction and housing, commerce and consumption. Also in the monetary sphere, there was an increase in the monetary base of only 15% at the same time as the monetary mass indicators, M2 and M3 grew by 40% and 50 %, respectively. In return, net credit to the government reached 480,000 million doubles, against 162,000 million the previous year, as a result of the increase in government depitos in 2008 by about 280 million billion fold. In 2008, the Central Bank decided to control liquidity through foreign exchange auctions (sales), a task made possible by close coordination with the Plico Treasury, keeping net international reserves above 4 months of imports. Ladies and gentlemen, One of our goals is to promote a sound, strong and competitive financial system. The Central Bank has been adopting a set of measures, aiming on the one hand the appropriation of some accepted international standards and, on the other, the dynamic of the national financial system. We have improved the financial sector's risk assessment instruments by improving the soundness of financial system indicators, reflected in the combined effort of the Central Bank, through banking supervision and credit institutions, by strengthening its internal management and control processes, as a way of addressing the various risks inherent in financial activity in general and banking in particular. However, the performance of banks has not been homogeneous in terms of efficiency and effectiveness. There has been an adverse evolution of some prudential ratios. Ladies and gentlemen, The increase in petreo and food prices on the international market has had a considerable impact on the domestic prices of fuel and food, which contributed to the deterioration of price levels, with inflation between 24-24.5% in 2008, however, a figure lower than in the previous two years. The external sector, at the mercy of relatively apathetic export growth, the export coverage rate has continued to deteriorate, accounting for 2% compared to 3.9% in 2007 this year, which requires further efforts to promote further diversification of our exports that must be done by increasing production towards the substitution of imports, as a condition to minimize external dependence on our economy. The foreign exchange market was greatly influenced by the oscillation of strong currencies in the international market, and the war doubled a depreciation of 5% compared to the give, against 9.9% recorded last year, reaching 15,000 Folds each North American Dar at the end of 2008. For the euro, the fold reversed the 22.5% depreciation curve recorded last year, with appreciation in certain months of the year. However despite ups and downs, at the end of the year 2008 quoted at the same value of the end of 2007, ie 21075 Doubles each Euro. The comfortable evolution of foreign reserves allowed covering more than 4 months of import of goods and services and thus contributed to a greater margin in the use of monetary and exchange rate policy instruments in order to ensure the stability of the foreign exchange market. It should be mentioned that in 2008 the BCSTP used for reasons of intervention in the foreign exchange market, about 10 million dares, a value higher than 2.1 and 6.4 million used respectively in 2007 and 2006. Ladies and gentlemen; The economic outlook for 2009, despite the uncertainties visible with the financial crisis we all know, appears favourable and we are convinced that the actions to be developed will be the most appropriate, and the institution will continue to be guided by a monetary and exchange rate policy that contributes to the macro-economic policy objectives set by the Government that provides for economic growth between 6 and 8%, a reduction in annual inflation to levels between 16 and 18%, as well as maintaining international reserves for a minimum of 4 months of imports of goods and services. The monetary programme for 2009 aims to keep the growth of the monetary base aligned with the objective of reducing inflation to expected levels. The weak financial intermediation and the high substitution of the fold by some foreign currencies impose serious limitations on the effectiveness of interest rates and other intervention instruments. We therefore have to rely first on budgetary restraint. Sassim, the Central Bank will continue to actively use foreign exchange auctions for liquidity control, with particular attention being paid to maintaining a level of external reserves. Also for the coming year, the Central Bank of S. Tome and Principe, as a supervisory body of the financial system, will continue to demand adequate surveillance to the indicators of soundness and stability of the financial system, taking into account the current situation of international crisis. In the same situation, the Central Bank has the prospect of making the Interbank Money Market operational, and of promoting efforts to introduce modern means of payment through ATMs and other automatic payment terminals. Also in this context, we have a view to modernizing the interbank information network and introducing the new Plan of Accounts for the Central Bank and the financial system. In the exchange rate, the exchange cooperation agreement between the Sao Tome and Portuguese Treasuries could be signed in order to ensure the convertibility of the Fold, through fixed parity against the Euro, as a way of granting greater confidence, stability and opportunities to our economy. Ladies and gentlemen We wish to express our deep gratitude to all the economic agents of the country, society in general and the international community for the valuable contribution they have made to us in carrying out our mission, particularly with regard to the formulation and implementation of a monetary and exchange rate policy that is in line with which we aim to achieve sustainable economic growth. Allow me to express special thanks to the workers of the national financial system and in particular to those of the Central Bank for the dedication and commitment shown throughout 2008. The year 2009 will be another year full of challenges and we believe that we will know how to face it with courage and determination. We are sure that our bets will be won for the good of the country and society at large. To all v, I wish a happy New Year's Eve, with good departures and better entries in the year that awaits us. Well be to all; Thank you very much

Title: Speech by Inauguration of OCBSTP
CentralBank: Central Bank of So Tom and Prncipe
text: GOVERNOR'S SPEECH ON THE OCCASION OF THE INAUGURATION OF THE OCEANIC BANK OF S.T.P. His Excellency, Mr President of the Republic, His Excellency, Mr President of the National Assembly, His Excellency, Your Excellency, Prime Minister and Head of Government, Your Excellency, Your Excellency, Mr President of the Court of Auditors, Honourable Members of the Government, Members of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank, Financial Institutions and Oceanic Bank of STP in In particular, Most Reverend Bishop of the Diocese of S.TomeePrincipe Distinguished Guests, Excellencies Ladies and gentlemen, let me, in brief words, make use of the opportunity offered to us by the inaugural occasion, which marks the institutionalization and entry of the Oceanic Bank of STP into our market, to allude to a date, which imposes itself on memorable and without which, it would be unthinkable our presence at this honorable event. Excellencies In just five years, fate has allowed us to witness changes in the national economic and financial fabric. Changes have not always been fruitful, just as good intentions have not always sufficed. However, the financial system in particular and the economy in general are too sensitive to instabilities and imbalances. Therefore, it takes a lot of commitment and dedication and much more determination in what we do. The formulas of banking in the past were simple and consisted of making government its ally, the national business partner and the national economy a point of arrival and not a starting point. Today, we have 8 banks, which the departure, makes us believe, that there will be prospects for economic growth, and poverty reduction in our country. Excellencies Ladies and gentlemen, to Dr. Cecilia Ibru, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Oceanic Bank of STP, to whom we express consideration and appreciation, we would like to greet you and through you to the entire Management of your Bank and to tell you that, in fact, what we expect from The Bank is creativity, innovation and compliance with the law. Despite the efforts already made in the last thirty years and ongoing structural reforms, we still have important and several challenges such as: -Overcoming technological delays and Know-how; -Development of economic infrastructure, urbanization and spatial planning. -Adoption of a market-oriented development strategy, where improving the competitiveness of the economy and its dynamic integration into the regional and global economy are the dominant focus of the main economic policies in the near future. It should be noted that at the level of the financial system there is also much to be done: -The Payment Media System should be developed, based on advances in available information technologies; -The interbank money market must be implemented as a preliminary stage for the emergence of other markets. Our vision of the future suggests that we are challenging economic and financial operators to face the possibility of turning St Thomas and Principe into an international financial, commercial and economic square, and therefore preparing for the ambitious objective. These premises of stp development require that innovative formulas for mobilising financial capital be found, through the establishment of a partnership between the public and private sectors, national and foreign, and also among the participants of the national financial system. All this, naturally assuming the transition from a development model based on public investments to a competitiveness-based model, and in this context the financial system is called upon to play a key role. Therefore, we hope from you a dynamic and aggressive attitude, that goes to the business, that supports it and proposes effective, sustained and innovative options and alternatives, making this its strategic ally. Finally, I would like, on behalf of the Central Bank of STP, and on my own, to reiterate our thanks to the promoters of the Oceanic Bank of STP for their commitment to the Santomenses economy and financial system and to cast successful vows in your activity. Thank you all so much for your attention. Made in S. Tome, at 7 August 2008 Governor Luis Fernando MOREIRA DE SOUSA

Title: Speech by Inauguration of the New Sat Insurance

text: Mr President of the Repblica, Mr Interim President of the National Assembly, Mr. Prime Minister and Head of the Exma Government. Madam President of the Supreme Court of Justice, Mr. Attorney General of The Repblica Mr. President of the Court of Auditors Exmos. Members of the Exmos Government. Members of the Diplomatic Corps Exmos. Ladies and gentlemen of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank Reverend Bishop of the Diocese of Sao Tome and Prince Exmo. Insurance Exmos. Members of the Board of Directors of Commercial Banks, gentlemen, business Dear Guests... Ladies, gentlemen As the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Financial System Regulatory and Supervisory Authority, it is an honor for me to participate in the inauguration of an investment that will henceforth be the headquarters of the Insurance Company Sat-Insurance in our country. As is common knowledge, Sao Tome e Principe already had a state insurance company, called Compensadora, extinct in the nineties. During the interregnum period that runs until 2002, there was a certain numbness with regard to the importance of the insurance activity, its role in the National Financial System and, in the context of macro-economic affirmation of the country as a whole. The monetary authority, recognizing the importance of this activity in the national context, at a time when it was preparing for the qualitative leap, through the dynamic of the private sector, created conditions in close collaboration with the Government, so that decree-law 47/98, which regulates the conditions of access to insurance activity, was published and establishes the rules of operation of the respective market. This effort culminated in the issuance of License No. 1/2001 dated 16 November in favour of Sat-Insurance. The insurance company that now inaugurates its new headquarters has authorization for the operation of Insurance in the General Branches. The inauguration of this building represents an important milestone for the national economy, because it is a sign that the private sector can contribute to the infrastructure of the country, so we call and encourage other financial institutions to go down the same path. It is common knowledge that the national market is incipient in this field of activity, so both the Central Bank and the Government and the General Directorate of Sat -Insurance itself, should operate all mechanisms aimed at the effective implementation of existing standards, as well as sensitize the general population to the advantages arising from the insurance sector. (Example: a country with an automotive park estimated at 9,000 vehicles, only 3,000, approximately, have compulsory insurance). Ladies, gentlemen The National Financial System has observed an expressive quantitative growth, due to the number of institutions that integrate it, however, it is not always accompanied by the necessary implementation of mechanisms that can diversify the services provided and, consequently, enhance the much desired level of competitiveness. In this context, the monetary authority, as a supervisory and supervisor of the national financial system, calls on the General Directorate of Sat Insurance in particular and other economic agents, potential promoters of the insurance activity, in order to intensify the direct and indirect mechanisms that could strengthen the Insurance Sector in Sao Tome and Principe. Despite the specificities of our market, measures have been adopted by the supervisory body with the aim of ensuring the strengthening of mechanisms for monitoring insurance activity. An example of this are the two draft Decree-Laws, one of partial reform of Decree-Law 47/98 and another project that aims to define the rules of domicile of insurance in Sao Tome and Principe (as an example of this last, in case of extraction of the oil in the area of joint exploitation between the Federal Republic of Nigeria and RDSTP the insurance of companies operating in the area will comply with the same sharing criteria, i.e. 60/40%). In the reform of Decree-Law 47/98, the highlight is the supervisory fee, the minimum social capital and the model of automvel liability card. Ladies and gentlemen On behalf of the Board of Directors of BCSTP and my own, let me express both the General Management of Sat  Insurance, and the potential promoters of the insurance activity, our full willingness to assist in any way necessary, aiming at boosting the activities carried out by these companies, guiding, as it could not fail to be, strict compliance with the laws, rules and regulations, which deal with the matter. We also call on the national authorities to cooperate with the insurance sector, so that the implementation of Decree  Law 30/2000, which regulates compulsory insurance, is more comprehensive. To finish I would like once again, on behalf of the Central Bank of S.T.P., and in my own, to reiterate our thanks to Sat-Insurance for its commitment to the National Financial System in particular, and in the economy as a whole, and to express our vows of success in your activity. Thank you very much

Title: Speech on the Occasion of the 16th Anniversary of bcstp
CentralBank: Central Bank of So Tom and Prncipe
text: SPEECH BY THE GOVERNOR ON THE OCCASION OF THE 16th ANNIVERSARY OF THE INSTITUTIONALIZATION OF BCSTP (1992-2008) Your Excellency Prime Minister and Head of Government, Your Excellency, Madam President of the Supreme Court, Your Excellency Mr Attorney General of the Republic, Your Excellency, Mr President of the Court of Auditors, Honourable Members of the Government, Your Honourable Judges of the Supreme Court, Members of the Diplomatic Corps, Members of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank and financial institutions, Heads of state directorates, private sector, NGOs and international bodies, Distinguished Guests, Your Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen, Firstly, I would like to thank you on behalf of the institution, and to congratulate you on the honorable presence of the most honorable people present for the fact that you have given us your appearance at this event which marks the commemoration of another anniversary of the institutionalisation of BCSTP, in this case the 16th (1992-2008). In an international framework of obvious global financial disruptions and characterized by global food crisis scenarios, the Central Bank of St. Thomas and Principe, in celebrating its anniversary, decided to organize this round table to reflect on the following topics. The theme is the "Contribution of the Banking Sector in Combating the Food Crisis", because it is a global problem, with a very negative impact on S. Tome and Principe. And the theme is the "Banking of the National Economy", which has to do with the form and size of penetration of banking services into the economy and the need to bring its population closer. The problem of the food crisis has been debated in all global economic for a with great seriousness, including in institutions such as FAO, the IMF, the World Bank and the ADB. In some of these forums, such as that held by the IMF and world bank in August 2007 in Maputo, and more recently in the capital of Mauritania, attention has been drawn to the need, especially for African countries, to allocate around 10% of their GDP to the agricultural sector. However, we know the difficulties inherent in this sector, fundamentally, when it comes to the high risk of recovery of investments, which makes it difficult for the banking to direct resources to the primary sector. In the meantime, we know of the extreme importance of the agricultural sector for the country, fundamentally, in a nation, predominantly agricultural like ours, and still very dependent on imported food. Excellencies Ladies and gentlemen Therefore, it is essential that everyone take on this challenge, which is to improve the performance of the agricultural sector, since it generates employment, stimulates the increase in income of the poorest populations, and consequently exposes the national income. However, an investment factor in the agricultural area should be reflected in conjunction with the banking factor of the economy, which, despite improvement, seems to be still very low. For various reasons that we are going to discuss here, economic transactions are mostly done in fiat currency, i.e. cash-free, including in foreign currency, with enormous costs arising from this practice. Informality in our economy is very high, which prevents banking from making its contribution to economic growth more effective, and the most affected sector appears to be agriculture, livestock and fisheries. Banking is still very concentrated in the capital city, which indicates that the use of cash is very high and inevitable, especially in areas where there is no representation and banking services. We also know that average household incomes are not very high, but we are called upon to find more appropriate ways and approaches to change the current framework of unbalanced geographical and demographic representation of banking. The Central Bank, together with the Government, and with the competition of the actors of the financial system and other state bodies, should look for better ways to stop the negative impact of the food crisis on the populations, and do everything to ensure that the banking will be of greater proportion in our country. Excellencies Ladies and gentlemen In just 5 years, we have seen an exponential evolution in the number of financial operators, reaching today 15 bank branches and an insurance company. It turns out, however, that enlargement in rural areas will continue to be the challenge that we must all mobilize. Our vision of the future suggests that we are challenging economic and financial operators to contribute more and better to the country's economic growth. Innovative formulas for mobilising financial capital must be found, through the establishment of partnerships between the public and private sectors, between NGOs and the financial sector, as well as partnerships between the actors of the national financial system to achieve this desideratum. Therefore, we expect from everyone, prudent but dynamic attitudes that stimulate greater entrepreneurship. Excellencies Ladies and gentlemen This clearly shows us that in order to reduce poverty and reach acceptable levels of human and social development, we will have to grow more than the current levels, which range from 6%, and the financial sector is of paramount importance in this process. Recognizing that in the banking process, currency stability is important, the BCSTP will continue efforts to stabilize the national currency, control inflation, step up supervision of the financial system and bet on modernization, the latter being a bet, with electronic payments. Finally, I would like, on behalf of the Central Bank of Sao Tome and Principe, and on my own, to reiterate our thanks to all, and to wish that at the end of this round table important conclusions and recommendations can come out which will best mobilize us for the objectives recommended. Thank you all so much for your attention. S. Tome, on 26 August 2008, The Governor

text: Econmic Balance of the Year 2008 Speech given by Mr. Governor of BCSTP Excellencies Ladies and gentlemen, Firstly, on behalf of myself and the Members of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of St. Thomas and Principe, I would like to thank you all at this traditional end-of-year meeting in which we take stock of the year that is about to end and present the prospects for the first year. We started 2008 in an adverse international situation, mainly due to the volatility of the petreo price, which reached the maximum of more than 150 Dares per barrel by mid-September 2008, against about 100 Dares of the year 2007. Fortunately, the signs that come to us at this end of the year feed us a certain optimism in this area, especially in the impact on cereal and petreo price levels, and this thymus is reaching values below 40 a barrel, but which contrasts with the financial crisis that currently affects the world. The current unstable international financial situation, due to the financial crisis that has increased and spread rapidly in this great quarter, has been observed by the Central Bank with some concern, and we are extremely concerned about its possible negative impact on the various spheres of national life, mainly in the economic and social spheres. S. Tome is Prince cannot therefore remain indifferent to this unfavourable international situation over which we have no control. Ladies and gentlemen, We are a small economy, inserted in the international market, dependent on the outside, not of import to meet much of our basic needs in food, energy and equipment, as well as in the financing plan the economy in general. Despite the very unfavorable international context, the Santomense economy proved to be, in the year that now ends, a moderate economic activity with GDP growing between 5 and 6%, that is, the same as in 2007. The construction sectors, associated with tourism, communications, trade, financial services, among other services, have contributed to this performance of GDP growth, which continued to be the main determinants of growth, adding to the momentum given by foreign direct investments. Despite this good performance of the GDP behavior of the previous years, the level of economic activity of the country is still little expressive and manifestly insufficient to enhance development and social well-being. It should be noted that cocoa exports have increased slightly as a result of their price increase on the world market, however, the contribution of the agricultural sector to economic growth remains rather weak. Ladies and gentlemen, A stable and competitive financial system can contribute decisively to economic growth and the necessary macro-economic stability, as it is of fundamental importance in supporting such key factors as investment, development, modernisation and innovation; conditions which, as we all know, are inseparable from the growth of our economy, currently living in an environment of globalisation. The importance of demand for credits is an example of how the financial system can enhance development, and this is justified by the increase in credit the economy, reaching a level of 639,000 million folds in the current year, against 619,000 million folds in the previous year. The sectors that benefited the most from this increase were construction and housing, commerce and consumption. Also in the monetary sphere, there was an increase in the monetary base of only 15% at the same time as the monetary mass indicators, M2 and M3 grew by 40% and 50 %, respectively. In return, net credit to the government reached 480,000 million doubles, against 162,000 million the previous year, as a result of the increase in government depitos in 2008 by about 280 million billion fold. In 2008, the Central Bank decided to control liquidity through foreign exchange auctions (sales), a task made possible by close coordination with the Plico Treasury, keeping net international reserves above 4 months of imports. Ladies and gentlemen, One of our goals is to promote a sound, strong and competitive financial system. The Central Bank has been adopting a set of measures, aiming on the one hand the appropriation of some accepted international standards and, on the other, the dynamic of the national financial system. We have improved the financial sector's risk assessment instruments by improving the soundness of financial system indicators, reflected in the combined effort of the Central Bank, through banking supervision and credit institutions, by strengthening its internal management and control processes, as a way of addressing the various risks inherent in financial activity in general and banking in particular. However, the performance of banks has not been homogeneous in terms of efficiency and effectiveness. There has been an adverse evolution of some prudential ratios. Ladies and gentlemen, The increase in petreo and food prices on the international market has had a considerable impact on the domestic prices of fuel and food, which contributed to the deterioration of price levels, with inflation between 24-24.5% in 2008, however, a figure lower than in the previous two years. The external sector, at the mercy of relatively apathetic export growth, the export coverage rate has continued to deteriorate, accounting for 2% compared to 3.9% in 2007 this year, which requires further efforts to promote further diversification of our exports that must be done by increasing production towards the substitution of imports, as a condition to minimize external dependence on our economy. The foreign exchange market was greatly influenced by the oscillation of strong currencies in the international market, and the war doubled a depreciation of 5% compared to the give, against 9.9% recorded last year, reaching 15,000 Folds each North American Dar at the end of 2008. For the euro, the fold reversed the 22.5% depreciation curve recorded last year, with appreciation in certain months of the year. However despite ups and downs, at the end of the year 2008 quoted at the same value of the end of 2007, ie 21075 Doubles each Euro. The comfortable evolution of foreign reserves allowed covering more than 4 months of import of goods and services and thus contributed to a greater margin in the use of monetary and exchange rate policy instruments in order to ensure the stability of the foreign exchange market. It should be mentioned that in 2008 the BCSTP used for reasons of intervention in the foreign exchange market, about 10 million dares, a value higher than 2.1 and 6.4 million used respectively in 2007 and 2006. Ladies and gentlemen; The economic outlook for 2009, despite the uncertainties visible with the financial crisis we all know, appears favourable and we are convinced that the actions to be developed will be the most appropriate, and the institution will continue to be guided by a monetary and exchange rate policy that contributes to the macro-economic policy objectives set by the Government that provides for economic growth between 6 and 8%, a reduction in annual inflation to levels between 16 and 18%, as well as maintaining international reserves for a minimum of 4 months of imports of goods and services. The monetary programme for 2009 aims to keep the growth of the monetary base aligned with the objective of reducing inflation to expected levels. The weak financial intermediation and the high substitution of the fold by some foreign currencies impose serious limitations on the effectiveness of interest rates and other intervention instruments. We therefore have to rely first on budgetary restraint. Sassim, the Central Bank will continue to actively use foreign exchange auctions for liquidity control, with particular attention being paid to maintaining a level of external reserves. Also for the coming year, the Central Bank of S. Tome and Principe, as a supervisory body of the financial system, will continue to demand adequate surveillance to the indicators of soundness and stability of the financial system, taking into account the current situation of international crisis. In the same situation, the Central Bank has the prospect of making the Interbank Money Market operational, and of promoting efforts to introduce modern means of payment through ATMs and other automatic payment terminals. Also in this context, we have a view to modernizing the interbank information network and introducing the new Plan of Accounts for the Central Bank and the financial system. In the exchange rate, the exchange cooperation agreement between the Sao Tome and Portuguese Treasuries could be signed in order to ensure the convertibility of the Fold, through fixed parity against the Euro, as a way of granting greater confidence, stability and opportunities to our economy. Ladies and gentlemen We wish to express our deep gratitude to all the economic agents of the country, society in general and the international community for the valuable contribution they have made to us in carrying out our mission, particularly with regard to the formulation and implementation of a monetary and exchange rate policy that is in line with which we aim to achieve sustainable economic growth. Allow me to express special thanks to the workers of the national financial system and in particular to those of the Central Bank for the dedication and commitment shown throughout 2008. The year 2009 will be another year full of challenges and we believe that we will know how to face it with courage and determination. We are sure that our bets will be won for the good of the country and society at large. To all v, I wish a happy New Year's Eve, with good departures and better entries in the year that awaits us. Well be to all; Thank you very much

Title: Speech on the Occasion of the 17th Anniversary of BCSTP
CentralBank: Central Bank of So Tom and Prncipe
text: SPEECH BY THE GOVERNOR ON THE OCCASION OF THE 17TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE INSTITUTIONALIZATION OF BCSTP (1992-2009) S.E., Acting President of the National Assembly, S.E.M. Prime Minister- Interim Minister, S.E.Senhor President of the Supreme Court, S.E.Senhor Attorney General of the Republic, S.E.Senhor President of the Court of Auditors, Honourable Members of the Government, S.E.Senhor Representative of the Presidency of the Republic, Honourable Members of the Diplomatic Corps, Members of the Bank's Board of Directors Central and Financial Institutions, Distinguished Guests Your Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen, First of all, I would like on behalf of BCSTP and on my own to thank you for having deigned to toast us with your honorable presence at this event that marks the commemoration of the 17th anniversary of the institutionalization of BCSTP. Today's day offers us a special opportunity for us to celebrate another year of life for the Central Bank in its struggle to fulfil its mission that led to its creation, but it must also be a day of reflection on the path taken and on the growing challenges facing the ever-increasing demands we face in an increasingly globalized world with its harmful effects. for weaker economies like ours. This is how the BCSTP could not remain indifferent to the persistent climate of degradation of the prospects for global growth, which, although indirectly, influences national economic and social performance. In view of the situation caused by the housing bubble in the world's largest economies, which had a strong impact on their economic performance and consequently on the weakest economies, the IMF revised down the outlook for global economic activity in 2009, with a 1.3% decline. In most European, American and Asian countries, the economic downturn still persists, and recovery is expected only for the year 2010. For the IMF Director, the international situation remains critical and it is too early to declare its end, despite some sign of recovery, such as: (a) a smaller decrease in economic activity than originally expected in the US and the Eurozone, b)Higher than expected growth in China's P.R., (c)growth of the Japanese economy, d)Recent confirmation of signs of recovery of the German Economy e)Economic growth of the least developed countries, Successive decreases in interest rates, primarily in the American economy, the Eurozone and R.P. China, have given and continue to give a crucial impetus for the recovery of global economic activity. As the Santomense economy is heavily dependent on the outside world economy, the contraction of the world economy can have an impact on the contribution of the OGE, primarily in the financing of public investment projects (PIP) and foreign direct investments (EI). Your Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen, Although indirectly and very light, the Financial System was also not indifferent to the negative effects of the global crisis, with the decrease in the yield of investments made in low-risk financial assets, following the decrease in interest rates in major international markets. The decrease in the capacity of the OGE derived primarily from exogenous factors has hampered actions to combat the food and social crisis. The problem of the food crisis has been debated very seriously since 2008 in various global economic for a, including in institutions such as FAO, imf, world bank and oBAD. Following several international discussions by international financial organisations, our international financial partners such as the World Bank, the IMF and the ADB/FAD have been looking for ways to finance the agricultural sector of highly vulnerable countries, and there are already positive signs for our country of this international will. At the level of contribution of the national financial sector in combating the crisis, the expansion of credit to the economy has been observed, derived from the process of diversification and competition, also linked to the factor of lower interest rates. In the last seven years, we have seen a strong evolution in the number of financial operators, currently reaching 18 bank branches and 2 insurers, and enlargement to the interior areas of the country is the challenge of interbank competition for the coming times. The Central Bank will continue its price stabilization effort by using the scarce instruments of intervention available in the money and foreign exchange market as efficiently as possible. The reduction of almost half of the annual inflation rate from 37% in July 2008 to 15.4% in July this year is clear evidence of this effort, which has been healy resemiable to the Government's fiscal restraint policy. The inflation accumulated this last July was 8.7%, the lowest in the last 6 years. International reserves remain above the levels desired internationally, i.e. more than 4 months of import of goods and services. The Central Bank will also continue to strive for better supervision of the financial system. The increased systematization of ongoing direct visits, the new programme for the direct assessment of credit portfolios and the implementation of an ongoing risk center are among other evidences of the Central Bank's increased engagement in monitoring banking and insurance activities. Once the technical and financial feasibility study for the implementation of an electronic automatic payment system is completed, a joint partnership owned by the banks and cst will soon be set up to take charge of the installation of a modern payment system in the country. The recent signing of the economic cooperation agreement with Portugal for exchange rate parity Dobra-Euro, which is scheduled to enter into force next January, is at the same time a great progress and a major challenge. In addition to maintaining a climate of macroeconomic rigour firmly, the implementation, with the support of cooperation partners, of an integrated development programme in order to overcome the main sources of structural imbalances still existing, especially in the productive and infrastructure sector, so that we can maintain the current trend of nominal convergence, as the only source of sustainability of this desideratum. Your Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen, The choice of the theme "Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing" for debate in this forum does not come by chance. The fight against money laundering is part of the national and international agenda, especially when due to lack of information the country has been blacklisted by an organization that monitors illicit operations. The level of transactions outside the financial system in our economy is still high, a phenomenon that is associated with the high level of informality of our economy. That is why we welcome and encourage the Government for the recent measures taken to support the banking of all financial operations in the state. The presence here in this forum of representatives of regional institutions linked to this issue (GIABA and Consultant Jose Carapinha of the Macau Financial Information Office) confirms our intention and determination, together with the International community, to combat all forms of organized crime and supported by financial transactions. Interpretive Notes and International Best Practices have been issued in relation to the Special Recommendations on Terrorist Financing, particularly with regard to bank transfers and alternative remittance systems. In the national financial sector, new regulations should be issued in parallel to the law on money laundering, namely i) the registration of foreign exchange transactions and (ii) exchange transactions, opening and movement of accounts in foreign currency in the national territory. In addition to the original requirement to verify the identification and retention of customer records, the first regulation will incorporate the need for customer acceptance policy and procedures, monitoring of high-risk customer accounts and adequate risk management. The second standard will regulate procedures for dealing with cash transactions involving large sums for all authorized institutions, including financial intermediaries, exchange offices and cash remittance companies. The creation of the Financial Information Unit is one of the decisive steps in this fight, so we hope that this will happen very with the establishment of a multi-sectoral team to ensure continuous monitoring of particularly relevant financial transactions. Our joint efforts should, I hope, be translated into the elimination of S. Tome and Principe on such a blacklist for the good of the national economy. Finally, I would like once again to reiterate our thanks to all, and to hope that at the end of this lecture important conclusions and recommendations can come out which will best mobilize us all to the objectives advocated. Our special thanks are addressed to the theme presenter, Consultant Jose Carapinha of the Macau Financial Information Office and also to the honorable presence of giaba representatives. Our thanks are also addressed to the Presidency, Parliament, the Government, the Courts and the Attorney General's Office. Thank you so much for your attention. S. Tome, on 26 August 2009, Governor Luis Sousa

Title: Economic Balance Speech of the Year 2009
CentralBank: Central Bank of So Tom and Prncipe
text: Econmic Balance of the Year 2009 Speech given by Mr. Governor of BCSTP Excellencies Ladies and gentlemen, Firstly, on behalf of myself and the Members of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of St. Thomas and Principe, I would like to thank you all at this traditional end-of-year meeting in which we take stock of another year which ends in which we also present the prospects for the following year. The year 2009 has already begun with a difficult international situation dragged last year. Fortunately, the signs from mid-2009 have fueled some optimism in this area, especially in the impact on food and petreo price levels, and this thymus is reaching figures of around 74 a barrel, but which contrasts with the financial crisis that currently affects the world. The current international financial situation, due to the financial crisis that has become rapidly accentuated since 2008, has been observed by the Central Bank with some concern. Despite signs of improvement, its negative impact on the various spheres of national life, especially in the economic and social spheres, is still felt. Ladies and gentlemen, We are a small economy, dependent on the outside world, not on the basic needs in food and energy goods and equipment, but also in the financing plan for the OGE in particular and financing the economy in general. Despite the very difficult international context, the Santomense economy proved to be a moderate economic activity in 2009 with GDP growing between 4 and 5%. They contributed to this growth, the financial sector associated with the construction, communications, trade, among others, which the likeness of the previous year continued to be the main determinants of growth, obviously adding to the momentum provided by foreign direct investments. Despite this good performance of the behaviour of these sectors of economic activity, they still remain insufficient to ensure quality and social well-being. It should be noted that cocoa exports have increased slightly as a result of increased production and the international price of biolico cocoa, although with little weight in GDP, that however, the contribution of the agricultural sector to national economic growth remains quite weak. Ladies and gentlemen, A stable, competitive and expanding financial system obviously contributes to encouraging economic growth and the necessary macro-economic stability, as it is of fundamental importance in supporting such essential factors as investment, consumption, development, modernisation and innovation of financial services and products; conditions which, as we all understand, are inseparable from the growth of any economy. The importance of demand for credits is an example of how the national financial system enhances development, and this is justified by the increase in credit the economy, reaching a level of 1052 million billion in the current year, against 754 thousand billion of folds in the previous year, with the Construction and Housing sectors, trade and consumption to benefit more from this increase. In contrast, net credit to the government reached 258,000 million folds, against 406 million doubles the previous year, as a result of the government's 2009 increase in the government's depitos by about 150,000 million folds. In 2009, the Central Bank decided to control liquidity through foreign exchange auctions, a task made possible by close coordination with the Plico Treasury, keeping net international reserves above 4 months of imports. Ladies and gentlemen, One of our objectives is to promote a sound, strong and competitive financial system. The Central Bank has been adopting a set of measures, aiming on the one hand the appropriation of some accepted international standards and, on the other, a greater dynamic of the national financial system. We have improved the financial sector's risk assessment instruments by improving the soundness of financial system indicators, reflected in the combined effort of the Central Bank, through banking supervision and credit institutions, by strengthening its internal management and control processes, as a way of minimizing the various risks inherent in financial activity in general and banking in particular. Excellencies The level of prices of petreo, its derivatives and food products on the international market has had a positive impact on domestic fuel and food prices, which added to monetary and budgetary control, have contributed to an improvement in domestic price levels, with inflation at between 15-16% in 2009, a figure much lower than in the previous seven years. The external sector, at the mercy of relatively apathetic export growth, the rate of export coverage of imports has continued to deteriorate, which requires additional efforts to promote further diversification of our exports, a desideratum, which must be achieved by increasing production towards the substitution of imports, as a condition for further economic dependence on our economy. The foreign exchange market was greatly influenced by the oscillation of strong currencies in the international market, and the war recorded a depreciation of 9.9% compared to the give, against 6% recorded last year, reaching 16,735 Folds each North At the end of 2009. For the euro, the fold aggravated the 1.7% depreciation curve recorded last year, having depreciated by 12.3% this year, which is all about the euro versus Dar's contribution on the international market, which in some periods of 2009 reached 1.5, compared to 1.35 in 2008. Against this justification, at the end of 2009, a Euro is 24,100 Doubles, compared to 21,940 Doubles in 2008. The comfortable evolution of foreign reserves has allowed us to cover more than 6 months of imports of goods and services and thus allowed for a greater margin in the use of monetary and exchange rate policy instruments in order to ensure the stability of the foreign exchange market, and to contribute to the sustainability of the economic cooperation agreement. It should be mentioned that in 2009 BCSTP used 12 times foreign exchange auctions, for reasons of market intervention, totaling about 13 million dares, when in 2008 out of 10 million folds. Ladies and gentlemen; Economic perspectives for the year 2010 The economic outlook for 2010, despite uncertainties, is beginning to show signs of improvement in the levels of large economies and we convince that the actions to be developed internally will be the most appropriate, and the institution will continue to be guided by a supervision and monetary policy that contributes to the objectives of macro-economic policy defined by the Government that provides for economic growth between 4 and 5%, a reduction in annual inflation to levels between 10 and 11%, as well as keeping international reserves at a minimum of 4 months of imports of goods and services. The weak financial intermediation and the high substitution of the fold by some foreign currencies impose serious limitations on the effectiveness of interest rates and other intervention instruments. So we have to rely primarily on the budgetary balance, because then we can control liquidity and maintain a level of external reserves. Also for the coming year, the Central Bank of S. Tome and Principe, as a supervisory body of the financial system, will continue to demand adequate surveillance to the indicators of soundness and stability of the financial system, taking into account the situation. In the same situation, the Central Bank aims to make the Interbank Money Market operational, and to continue to promote efforts, aiming at the introduction of modern means of paymentthrough the installation of ATMs and other automated payment terminals in the first half of 2010. We have already started the process of modernizing the interbank information network and updating the central bank's information system. In the exchange rate field, the economic cooperation agreement signed between the Sao Tome and Portuguese Treasuries will enter into force on 1 January 2010 in order to ensure the convertibility of the Fold, through a fixed parity against the Euro, as a way of granting greater confidence, stability and opportunities to the Santomense economy. Title: Speech on the occasion of the 18th Anniversary of BCSTP
