text: SPEECH BY THE GOVERNOR ON THE OCCASION OF THE VTH MEETING OF THE GOVERNORS OF THE CENTRAL BANKS OF THE CPLP AND MACAU AND THE 18TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE INSTITUTIONALIZATION OF BCSTP (1992-2010) S.E,Mr President of the National Assembly, S.E. Mr Prime - Minister and Head of Government, S. E. Mr President of the Supreme Court, S.E. Mr Attorney General of the Republic, S. E. Mr President of the Court of Auditors, Honourable Members of the Government, Honourable Members of the Parliamentary Benches and Members, Honourable Members of the Diplomatic Corps, Distinguished Governors and representatives of the Central Banks of the CPLP and Macao, Members of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank and financial institutions, Dignissimos Guests Excellencies Ladies and gentlemen, First of all, I would like on behalf of BCSTP and in my own need to thank you for having deigned to toast us with your honorable presence at this event that marks the commemoration of another anniversary of the institutionalization of BCSTP, in this case its 18th and the Fifth Meeting of the Governors of the Central Banks of the CPLP and Macau. Today's day offers us a particular opportunity to celebrate together another year of life of the Central Bank in its struggle to fulfil the mission that led its creation, and it is also a day of reflection on the path taken and on the growing challenges that arise to us in the face of the ever- increasing demands we have to face in an increasingly globalized world with its diverse effects and for weaker economies like ours. This is how the BCSTP could not remain indifferent as it has always excelled, at this particular moment in view of the unknowns still existing in the growth prospects of the world economy that directly or indirectly influences national economic and social performance. In some European, American and Asian countries some signs of economic recovery are already appearing, but for many countries the situation remains critical and the end date is still uncertain. Since the Santomense economy is heavily dependent on abroad, uncertainties about the performance of the world economy can have an impact on the difficulties of the Performance of the OGE, primarily in the financing of public investment projects (PIP) and foreign direct investments (EI). Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen, The decrease in the capacity of the OGE derived fundamentally from exogenous factors has hindered the actions recommended by the State. Following several international discussions, our financial partners such as the World Bank, the IMF, the ADB/FAD among others have been looking for ways to finance the social sectors. At the level of contribution of the national financial sector to economic and social development, the economy has been clearly observed in the expansion of credit, derived from the process of diversification and competition, also linked to the factor of falling interest rates. In the last 10 years, we have seen a significant evolution in the number of financial operators, currently reaching a total of 20 bank branches and 2 insurers, and the extension to the interior areas of the country is the challenge of interbank competition for the coming times. The Central Bank of S. Tome and Principe will continue the effort to stabilize prices, using the scarce instruments of intervention available more efficiently. The reduction of almost 1/3 of the annual inflation rate, which went from 37% in July 2008 to 15.4% in July 2009 and to 12.4% in July 2010, is clear evidence of this effort, which has been healy counting on the government's fiscal restraint policy combined with restrictive monetary policy. The inflation accumulated this last July was 5.3%, the lowest in the last 7 years. International reserves maintain above the levels desired internationally, being above 5 months of import of goods and services. The Central Bank will also continue to strive for better supervision of the financial system. The increased systematization of ongoing direct visits, the new programme for direct assessment of credit portfolios and implementation of an ongoing risk center are among other evidence of our engagement in monitoring banking and insurance activity. After completing in 2008 the technical and financial feasibility study for the implementation of an electronic automatic payment system, a company was formed by bcstp, banks and CST to take charge of the installation of a modern payment system in the country in 2010. For various reasons, economic transactions are mostly carried out in fiat currency, i.e. with cash, including foreign currency movement, with enormous costs arising from this practice. The signing in July 2009 of the economic cooperation agreement with Portugal for exchange rate parity Dobra  Euro, whose last January came into force, was a great progress and a great challenge. This agreement implies, in addition to maintaining a climate of macroeconomic rigour, the implementation, with the support of cooperation partners, of an integrated development programme in order to overcome the main sources of structural imbalances still existing, especially in the productive and infrastructure sector, so that we can maintain the current trend of nominal convergence as the only source of sustainability of this desideratum. Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen, The choice of the theme "The role of the Financial Sector in Economic and Social Development" for debate at the CPLP Governors' Meeting is part of the national and international agenda, especially when today the creation of regional networks and economic groups are fundamental parts for cooperation and development of countries and consequently their populations. The level of transactions outside the financial system in our economy is still high, a phenomenon that is associated with the high level of informality of our economy. That is why we welcome the Government for the measures taken to support the banking of all financial operations in the state, which has opened up greater opportunities for the Santomenses and banking businesses on the one hand, and on the other hand better control of the state's financial operations. The presence here at this V meeting of Governors of the representations of our Central Banks confirms our intention and determination to, together with the International community, exchange experiences related to the level of progress of our Central Banks, in addition to providing more information to our community, among other aspects. Our joint efforts should be reflected in closer cooperation between the different countries of the community in financial and supervisory matters. Informality in our economy still exists, despite investment efforts, which in some way prevents banking from making its contribution to economic growth and social well-being more effective. Similarly, banking is still very concentrated in the capital city, despite the assumption of this task by decentralised banks, which indicates that the use of cash is very high. We also know that average household incomes are not very high, but we are called upon to find more appropriate ways and approaches to change the current framework of unbalanced geographical and demographic representation of banking and insurance. It turns out, however, that enlargement in rural areas will continue to be the challenge that we must all mobilize in the near future. Innovative formulas for mobilising financial capital must be found, through the establishment of partnerships between the public and private sectors, between NGOs and the financial sector, as well as partnerships between the actors of the national financial system to achieve this desideratum. Therefore, we advise everyone, prudent but dynamic attitudes that stimulate greater entrepreneurship. Excellencies My ladies and gentlemen This clearly shows us that in order to reduce poverty and reach acceptable levels of human and social development, we will have to grow more than the current levels, which fluctuate at 6%, and the financial sector is of paramount importance in this process. Recognizing that in the banking process, stability is important, THE BCSTP will continue efforts to control inflation, intensify the supervision of the financial system and bet on modernization, the latter being a bet, with tools that will allow us to quickly have an x-ray of the indicators of the national financial and economic system. Finally, I would like once again to reiterate our thanks to all, and wish that at the end of this Year. conclusions and recommendations and important measures that will best mobilise us for the objectives advocated. Thank you so much for your attention. S. Tome, on 26 August 2010, Governor Luis Sousa

Os nossos esfor<8d>os conjuntos dever<8b>o traduzir-se no estreitamento da coopera<8d><8b>o entre os diferentes pa<92>ses da comunidade em mat<8e>ria financeira e de supervis<8b>o. A informalidade na nossa economia ainda existe, apesar de esfor<8d>os de bancariza<8d><8b>o levado a cabo, o que impede de certa forma a banca de tornar mais eficaz a sua contribui<8d><8b>o ao crescimento econ<97>mico e bem-estar social. Da mesma forma, a banca est<87> ainda muito concentrada na cidade capital, apesar da assun<8d><8b>o desta tarefa pelos bancos de descentraliza<8d><8b>o, o que nos indica que a utiliza<8d><8b>o de numer<87>rio seja muito elevada. Sabemos tamb<8e>m que os rendimentos m<8e>dios das fam<92>lias n<8b>o s<8b>o muito elevados, mas, somos chamados a encontrar formas e abordagens mais adequadas para modificar o actual quadro de desequilibrada representa<8d><8b>o geogr<87>fica e demogr<87>fica da banca e seguros. Acontece por<8e>m, que o alargamento as zonas rurais continuar<87> a ser o desafio que nos deve mobilizar a todos nos pr<97>ximos tempos. H<87> que se encontrar f<97>rmulas inovadoras de mobiliza<8d><8b>o de capital financeiro, atrav<8e>s do estabelecimento de parcerias entre o sector p<9c>blico e o privado, entre as ONG<ab>s e o sector financeiro, al<8e>m de parcerias entre os intervenientes do sistema financeiro nacional para atingirmos este desiderato. Por isso, aconselhamos a todos, atitudes prudente, mas, din<89>micas que estimulem maior empreendedorismo. Excel<90>ncias Minhas senhoras e meus senhores Isto nos demonstra claramente que para reduzir a pobreza e atingirmos os patamares de desenvolvimento humano e social aceit<87>vel, teremos que crescer mais do que os actuais n<92>veis, que oscilam nos 6%, e o sector financeiro tem uma import<89>ncia capital neste processo. Reconhecendo que no processo de bancariza<8d><8b>o, a estabilidade <8e> importante, o BCSTP vai continuar os esfor<8d>os para controlar a infla<8d><8b>o, intensificar a supervis<8b>o do sistema financeiro e apostar na moderniza<8d><8b>o, sendo esta <9c>ltima aposta, com ferramentas que nos permita rapidamente termos uma radiografia dos indicadores do sistema financeiro e econ<97>mico nacional. Para terminar, gostaria, mais uma vez, de reiterar os nossos agradecimentos a todos, e desejar que no fim deste V<bc>. encontro, possam sair conclus<9b>es e recomenda<8d><9b>es al<8e>m de importantes medidas que melhor nos mobilizar<87> para os objectivos preconizados. Muito obrigado pela vossa aten<8d><8b>o. S. Tom<8e>, ao 26 Agosto de 2010, O Governador Lu<92>s Sousa

Title: Economic Balance Sheet 2010
CentralBank: Central Bank of So Tom and Prncipe
text: Econmic Balance of the Year 2010 Speech given by the Governor of BCSTP Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen Firstly, on behalf of myself and the Members of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of St. Thomas and Principe, I would like to thank you all at this traditional end-of-year meeting in which we take stock of another year that ends and we also present the prospects for the following year. The current difficult international financial situation, due to the financial crisis that has become rapidly and spread since 2008 around the world, has been observed by the Central Bank with some concern. Despite some signs of improvement, its negative impact on the various spheres of national life, especially in the economic and social sphere, is felt. We are an economy, dependent on the outside, not only on the basic needs in food and energy goods and equipment, but also in the financing plan for the General State Budget (OGE) in particular and on financing the economy in general. Nevertheless, in this very difficult international context, the Santomense economy proved to be a moderate economic activity in 2010, with gross domestic product (GDP) growing above 4.5%, higher than the 4% recorded in 2009. They have contributed to this growth, the financial sector associated with the construction, consumption and trade sectors among others, which, like in recent years, have continued to be the main determinants of growth, obviously adding to the momentum provided by foreign direct investments. Despite the good performance of the behaviour of these sectors, they are still insufficient to ensure the quality and social well-being of the Santomenses. It should be noted that cocoa exports increased slightly as a result of increased production and the international price of organic cocoa, even though with little weight in GDP. The same has also happened with vanilla and pepper prices, however, the contribution of the agricultural sector to the balance of trade transactions remains quite derisory when compared to other sectors that contribute to growth. Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen, A competitive, expanding and stable financial system obviously contributes to encouraging economic growth and the necessary macroeconomic stability, as it is of fundamental importance in supporting such key factors as investment, consumption, modernisation and innovation of financial services and products; conditions that, as we all understand, are inseparable from the growth and development of any economy. The importance of demand for credits is an example of how the national financial system enhances development, and this is justified by the increase in credit to the private sector which reached a level above 1500 billion doubles in the current year, compared to 995 billion doubles in the previous year, with the Construction and Housing sectors, trade and consumption to benefit more from this increase. Similarly, net credit to the government reached 109 billion doubles as a result of the increase in credit to the Government by about 100 billion doubles. The Central Bank has been adopting a set of measures, aiming on the one hand to appropriate some internationally accepted standards on the supervision of the financial sector and, on the other hand, to further promote a sound, strong and competitive financial system. We have improved the financial sector's risk assessment instruments by improving the soundness of financial system indicators, reflected in the combined effort of the Central Bank, through banking supervision and credit institutions, by strengthening their internal management and control processes, as a way of minimising the various risks inherent in the financial activity itself in general and banking in particular, implementation of the credit risk center. Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen, Restrictive monetary and fiscal policy has contributed to an improvement in domestic price levels, with inflation falling below 13% in 2010, still below that recorded in the last 7 years. The external sector, at the mercy of relatively apathetic export growth, the rate of export import coverage has continued to deteriorate below 10%, which requires further efforts to promote further diversification and increase in our exports, a desideratum, which must be achieved by increasing production towards the substitution of imports, as a condition to de-aggravate the external dependence of our economy. The foreign exchange market was greatly influenced by the oscillation of strong currencies in the international market, and Dobra in 2010 recorded a depreciation of 10% against the Dollar, equivalent to last year, reaching 18,790.00 U.S. Dollar, against 16,815.00 doubles in 2009. It should be noted that the depreciation of the Fold against the dollar was mainly due to the depreciation of the Euro against the Dollar on the international market by about 9% during the year 2010, having quoted each Euro at 1.43 USD at the end of 2009 against 1.31 on 28 December of this year. Also in relation to the Euro, the country entered a fixed exchange regime since last January, through the economic cooperation agreement established between the treasures of Portugal and S. Tome and Principe where the exchange rate of Dobra against the Euro was fixed at 24,500.00. The comfortable evolution of foreign reserves allowed to cover more than 5 months of import of goods and services, thus granting a greater margin to the Central Bank in the use of monetary and exchange exchange policy instruments, in order to ensure price stability. Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen, In recent years, we have seen a significant evolution in the number of financial operators, currently reaching a total of 20 bank branches and 2 insurers, and the extension to the interior areas of the country is the challenge for competition in the financial sector in the near future. The Central Bank will also continue to strive for better supervision of the financial system. The systematization of ongoing direct visits and the new direct credit portfolio assessment programme, among others, are evidence of our engagement in monitoring the financial sector. After completion of the technical and financial feasibility study for the implementation of an automated electronic payment system, a company called SPAUT (Automated Payment System Management Company) was established, with the participation of BCSTP, commercial banks and CST, with the purpose of installing and managing a more modern, fast and effective payment system in the country. For various reasons, economic transactions are still mostly done in fiat currency, i.e. through cash, including foreign currency movement, with enormous costs arising from this practice, a phenomenon that is still associated with the high level of informality of our economy. In the foreign exchange market, the Central Bank has made a depending on how directly it will intervene by selling foreign currency to commercial banks according to their needs and the needs of economic operators. Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen, To reduce poverty and reach acceptable levels of human and social development, our economy will have to grow more than current levels, and we have a posture of more work, dedication and responsibility. Fiscal performance was positively reflected in the monetary sphere, with Net Credit to the Government having only a moderately expansionary impact on overall liquidity. Thus, the global monetary base contracted by 8%, while the monetary base in national currency grew by 59%, reflecting, however, the impact of the new regulation that implies the reconstitution of banks' mandatory bank reserves with the Central Bank only in national currency. We must not lose sight of the risks of external shocks to which the national economy is subject, which makes it potentially and delicately vulnerable, and therefore demanding permanent and courageous structuring measures until the main macroeconomic imbalances are minimised. For this reason, the process of consolidating and relaunching the national economy will require increasing efforts of cross-sectoral coordination, greater discipline and greater rigour in budgetary, monetary and fiscal management, as well as obviously the external support that is fundamental. Therefore, the prospects for the entry of external resources of our partners, may result in an important multiplier, associated with improvements in levels of confidence in the national economy. On the part of the monetary authority, as a way of granting commercial banks greater scope for financial intermediation and thus improving the business climate in the country, we announce today's decision to reduce the RMC coefficient from 24.5% to 23%, effective from next February, and a possible decrease in June 2011, monetary conditions are favoured. Economic perspectives for 2011 Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen; The economic outlook for 2011, with the uncertainties still in the world economies, is not very encouraging, given the measures to reduce consumption of households and businesses that condition economic activity and consequently economic growth. Therefore, actions to be internally engendered should be the most appropriate and the Central Bank will continue to be guided by a policy that contributes to the objectives of macroeconomic policy set by the Government that foresees economic growth above 5%, a reduction in annual inflation to levels between 7 and 8%, as well as maintaining international reserves at a minimum of 4 months of imports of goods and services. The improvement in financial intermediation and the strengthening of the use of the national currency  Dobra  are encouraging to us, and the latter in the past has imposed serious limitations on the effectiveness of the already scarce intervention instruments available. We therefore have to rely primarily on the budgetary and monetary balance, because only in this way can we control liquidity and maintain a solid level of external reserves, a fundamental basis for maintaining the economic cooperation agreement. Also for the coming year, the Central Bank of S. Tome and Principe, as a supervisory body of the financial system, will continue to demand enhanced surveillance of the indicators of soundness and stability of the financial system. Similarly, the Central Bank, together with the Government, aims to make the Interbank Money Market operational in the near future, as a way of using savings from the financial system for investments on the one hand, and on the other hand, the control of monetary liquidity for the purposes of internal price stability. The system of ATMs and technology terminals for the purchase of goods and payment of commercial, financial and public services will enter into operation by the end of January 2011, which will reduce the huge queues at bank branch branches and allow for greater efficiency in the financial sector. To last, we would like to express our deep gratitude to the national authorities, to all economic actors in the country, to society in general and to the international community for the valuable contribution they have made to us in carrying out our mission, particularly with regard to the formulation and implementation of a monetary and exchange rate policy in line with which we aim to achieve sustainable economic growth. Allow me to express special thanks to the workers of the national financial system and in particular those of the Central Bank of St. Thomas and Principe for the dedication and commitment shown throughout 2010. The year 2011 will be another year of challenges and we are sure that we will be able to face it with courage and determination and that our bets will be won for the good of St. Thomas and Principe. To all, I wish you a happy New Year's Eve and good entries for the year 2011. Thank you very much Luis De Sousa DECEMBER 2010

Title: Afriland First Bank Inauguration Speech

text: 31/03/2011 Excellencies Ladies and gentlemen, In delivering these brief words in this opening act, I can remember the constraints that involved the entry of Afriland First bank into our market, when stakeholders (investors and the Central Bank) had to share some uncertainties and risks. The Afriland Group had to set uncertain paths to invest in an economy it did not know about, while the Central Bank, in turn, took the risk of allowing this institution to open its doors to the public, without investing in fixed capital, despite the scepticism of some quarters of public opinion. The inauguration 2 years ago of the sat insurance office and today of this magnificent building is proof that it is possible in the financial sector to take calculated risks without necessarily being adventurous. I am sincerely proud to have been part of this process. It was worth the weighting and flexibility. I would like, with a loud voice, to congratulate you, mr. shareholders and directors of Afriland, for having honoured the commitments made and to thank you for toasting our avenue with this magnificent building. This reinforces unequivocally my conviction that South-South cooperation is possible and should be encouraged. I urge the Afriland Group to the challenge of finding other forms of cooperation with the Sao Tome economy, taking into account the ideals it defends and the multifaceted experience and knowledge it has accumulated on the African continent and our country. Excellencies Ladies and gentlemen, I would like to take this happy opportunity, to also share with you some convictions: There is no doubt that the national financial system is evolving. Having gone through the growth phase, the challenge hereafter is to consolidate and modernize. The contribution of banking has been undeniable in our economy. But we need to go further. We need to support and foster other sectors of economic activity, in addition to trade and construction. Do not touch the smallness of the economy, nor the slight light of our daily lives. I am convinced that when the moon has not yet gone in an economy, there is always an unexplored market segment and a new product that can be offered. Hence our call to be original, to seek creative mechanisms of partnership and risk sharing and to meet the business. The consolidation of the national banking system, in this context of crisis, will require more creativity from bank managers, always bearing in the information of the principles and values inherent in banking activity that must be preserved and the necessary balance of interests of the parties involved: shareholders, depositors and the economy. On the side of the Central Bank, there is a commitment to do everything possible for banking activity to contribute more and more to the development of the economy and the country. Finally, On behalf of the Central Bank, I would like to reiterate to the Afriland Group our thanks for their trust in our economy. Well there is AfrilandBank! Thank you so much.

Title: Economic Balance Speech of the Year 2012
CentralBank: Central Bank of So Tom and Prncipe
text: International conjuncture The international situation continued to be marked by the global economic and financial crisis. The main highlights are less robust growth in the United States, a fragile recovery in the Eurozone and a slowdown in economic activity in emerging countries. In sub-Saharan Africa, economic conditions remained stable despite the deterioration of the global economy and slowing growth in many middle-income countries with strong links to the markets of advanced economy countries. Macroeconomic policies were accommodating. Inflation has regressed compared to 2011 levels, thanks to the adoption of a more restrictive monetary policy in several countries in the region and an end to drought in the Sahel. On the supply side, stand out (i) the recovery of agricultural production in the Sahel and Kenya, (ii) the increase in oil production in several countries (Angola, Chad and Nigeria) and (iii) new natural resource exploration projects (e.g. Mozambique, Sierra Leone) Sub-Saharan Africa's financial systems have not suffered significant direct shocks from the crisis. There was, however, a downward trend in bank asset sums and capital due, among others, to losses in the loan portfolio and increased competition in some markets. Noteworthy is the maintenance of the downward trend of the ratio of low-for-r and the improvement of the solvency ratio According to the IMF, Angola and Mozambique stand out among the PALOP with better positioned financial health ratios. Internal economic conjuncture The macroeconomic, structural and socio-economic weaknesses of STP are profound. These weaknesses are reflected, among others, in a economic structure totally dependent on the outside world; on a chronically deficit balance of payments; in a level of external indebtedness, which despite the debt forgiveness that occurred in 2007, is again growing worryingly; in incipient social and productive infrastructures and/or with a high level of idleness; a still embryonic business fabric with poor job creation capacity. Despite these constraints, the economy has, in recent years, made some progress, these progress, framed by several government initiatives of which are more recent examples the Economic Cooperation Agreement signed with Portugal, the National Poverty Reduction Strategies (ENRP) and the economic adjustment programs supported by the IMF. Thus, in 2012, the evolution of the macroeconomic environment was in line with this dynamic, i.e. the slowdown in inflationary cadence, a moderate expansion of liquidity, the deepening of fiscal consolidation and a moderate pace of growth. One of the relevant aspects of the macroeconomic environment in 2012 was the low volume of external financing that conditioned the country's ability to make public investments and the level of foreign exchange reserves in the country. In order to address this situation, measures to contain OGE and other expenditure to improve exchange rate management were worth taking care of and which were decisive in ensuring macroeconomic stability. Among the relevant events of the year, the following are worth mentioning:  Approval in July of the new National Poverty Reduction Strategy for the period 2012-2016 that earned us the approval in July of a new IMF-supported adjustment programme under the Extended Credit Facility (ECF) and the disbursement of USD 4,200,000 for direct budget support;  Approval in September of an austerity package, focused on current expenditure, with a view to counterbalancing budgetary implementation difficulties in the face of international constraints;  setting profit margins on the marketing of nine food products in order to combat price speculation of such products considered essential; The main highlights of the conjuncture in 2012 are the fall, albeit timid, of inflation, which is expected to be close to 10%, in cumulative terms. This level of inflation is still high and reflects the volatility of the internal conjuncture due to different exogenous factors. This was the case in the second half of the year when inflation rose again as a result of the difficulties arising from the domestic supply of basic food. The smaller, than expected flow of external resources to the OGE resulted in a slowdown in economic activity and led to a lower revision of the economic growth outlook initially forecast for this year. Neverthemore, it is estimated that economic activity has preserved a level of growth of around 4%, supported mainly by the tertiary (telecommunications, banking and tourism) and primary (agriculture and livestock) sectors. Financial system In 2012, the financial system maintained its growth and modernization momentum. . An investment bank and three other bank branches came into operation. . We continue efforts to decentralise the banking network. There is currently at least one bank branch in 4 of the 6 Districts and rap; . The banking rate maintains its pace of improvement, currently close to 40%; . We continue the process of modernising the means of payment with the entry into operation of the Payment Terminals . With the object of protecting customers in the banking sector, the Central Bank issued a Standard on "Protection of Financial System Clients" that establishes a set of mandatory compliance rules. . On the other hand, we trigger the process of regulating the use of checks and microcredit activities, pending only the approval of the Government Despite this dynamic, the financial sector continues to face some constraints. The process of financial intermediation continues to be affected by the institutional difficulties facing banking and the interest rates of the banking system remain high, despite the reduction in the central bank's reference rate, On the other hand, the financial sector also absorbed the impact of the weak economic dynamism observed in the year. The profitability of the banking system's assets resented factors such as the decrease in turnover and is 1.5, slightly below that recorded last year. As a result of the financial difficulties of economic operators, there was an increase in the credit in rrear. The latest estimates point to an increase of 5 percentage points compared to last year, at around 20%, which in turn conditioned the banking system's ability to lend new loans. For this reason, credit to the economy had a modest increase of about 9% over the year. Outlook for 2013 remains uncertain. The risk of the economic situation worsening continues to hang in the forecasts of that institution, which in fact sees with great reserve the economic recovery of the Eurozone. Emerging countries will continue to play a relevant role, taking on the driving role in global growth. Sub-Saharan Africa is expected to maintain solid growth for 2013, which is expected to be around 5.3% (well above other regions). Internally, our actions in 2013 will take into account these forecasts, the prevailing risks on the international market and the macroeconomic objectives of the Government programme, which, although still under preparation, will certainly take into account the Triennial Adjustment Programme signed with the IMF/WB and the Economic Cooperation Agreement signed with Portugal. From this perspective, in 2013 fiscal consolidation efforts should be maintained with a view to ensuring the macroeconomic stability framework that is essential to maintain fixed exchange rate parity and improve the business environment. As part of our main functions as the Central Bank of STP, we will continue to manage monetary policy with a view to consolidating low inflation targets, in a fixed exchange rate regime and prioritizing the robust real growth of our economy that is expected to be between 4.0-4.5%. We will continue efforts to improve supervision, step up measures to protect customers and ensure the external credibility of the system as a whole; We will follow up measures to modernise the means of payments, taking advantage of the potential of the Dobra 24 Network and We will strengthen our statistical production base and make economic and financial information available to the public and thus contribute to improving financial literacy in the country.

text: Prime Minister and Head of Government, Excellency, Venerating Judge Councillor, President of the Supreme Court of Justice and Court Constitutional, Excellency, Venerable Judge Councillor, President of the Court of Auditors, Excellency, Minister for Finance, Trade and The Blue Economy, Distinguished Members of government, Excellencies, Your Chief Judge, Of the Court of First Instance, Your Excellese Executive Secretary, CPLP, Distinguished Members of the Diplomatic Corps and International Organizations, Mr President of the Regional Government, Distinguished Madam President and Distinguished Presidents of the District Chambers, Mr President of the BCSTP Audit Board, Distinguished members of the BCSTP Board of Directors, Distinguished members of the Board of Directors, Executive Committee and General Directorate of Financial Institutions, Other Civil, Religious and Military Entities and all protocol observed, Dear BCSTP Collaborators, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, Allow me, at this moment of celebration, to begin by greeting, in my name and in the Bcstp's Board of Directors, your presence at this ceremony. In using the floor on this occasion, I would like to thank the Prime Minister and Head of Government in an exquisite way for accepting the invitation to preside over this act. I am pleased to welcome the different individualities present in this solemnity that marks the highlight of the festivities alusive to the 25th anniversary of the institutionalization of the Central S. Tome and Principe. I would like to particularly greet Dr. Maria do Carmo Silveira, Executive Secretary of the CPLP, who made her available to participate in this event, which greatly honors us. I also take this opportunity to express our deep gratitude to all national and foreign partners, bilateral and multilateral, whose collaboration has contributed to the successful fulfillment of our mission as Central Bank of the Democratic Republic of St. Thomas and Principe. My words of appreciation extend, in particular, to the financial institutions operating in the country, whose valuable partnership we recognize in the implementation of policies pursuing sublime objectives of macroeconomic stability with positive social impact in terms of banking and inclusive development of the financial system. In making use of the prerogative offered to me on this occasion, loaded with symbolism for the Central Bank and for the country, I would like to make some considerations around the twenty-five years of our institution, full of challenges and great achievements. As the great Castilian poet Antonio Machado said, "the path is made by walking". Throughout its existence, the BCSTP has trodden the path of safeguarding macroeconomic stability, a necessary condition for the normal functioning of the economy and indispensable for the achievement of economic growth objectives, without ever disdecorating its obligations, although some constraints have been made on this path. The development effort of S. Tome and Principe, recognized in various titles, largely incorporates the contribution of the Central Bank, in the framework of the stability of the Fold and the national financial system, in its robes as supervisor of the financial sector and, more recently, as a resolution entity of banking institutions. As a monetary and exchange rate authority, BCSTP has participated in the incessant search for solutions to address the inconsistencies of exchange rate regimes in relation to the country's economic context. Indeed, in the last seven years monetary policy has been oriented towards safeguarding the credibility of the fixed exchange rate regime between Dobra and Euro, thus ensuring the country's exchange rate stability, with visible gains, both in terms of nominal convergence and stability of the national currency. Inflation continued its trend towards historic lows, suggesting a clear comparative advantage in the regional context. However, it is an asset that can be consolidated and maximized, with the paradigm shift to an economy dedicated to domestic production and export, in favor of improving the business environment. The Central Bank will remain committed to its main objective, which is to ensure low and stable inflation, because we believe this is the way in which we become more competitive in the attraction of new investments, in addition to preserving the purchasing power of families with lower incomes, thus contributing to the fight against poverty. In view of the constraints that continue to postpone the diversification of the economy towards increasing export capacity, and bearing in mind that we have not yet achieved economic self-sufficiency, one of the challenges of the Central Bank as a monetary and exchange rate authority, is the maintenance of international reserves at levels compatible with the exchange rate regime in force. In view of the need to strengthen the adequacy of profiles to the functions performed and, thus, to promote the Participation of the Bank in the country's development effort, considerable changes were made to the operational and management structure, developed skills, expanded the instruments of analysis and improved the human resources of our institution. Twenty-five years later, the growth of the Santomense financial sector is very noticeable, the expansion of financial services and products is visible, and the evolution of national payment systems and other indicators of the sector's scope is indisputable. However, it must be acknowledged that there is still a long way to go, especially with regard to the convergence of the sector with international standards, and we hope that progress in the national financial system will make a greater difference in the lives of each Saint. The dynamics of economic activity, an indispensable presupposition for maintaining macroeconomic stability, also depends to a large extent on the level of trust, credibility and perkity of the national currency, undoubtedly one of the symbols of our country's sovereignty. Dobra was adopted by combining Decree-Law 23/76, 50/76 27/77 and 28/77. Since then, precisely forty years ago, our currency has been accompanying us as an instrument of exchange, means of payment and reserve value, so it is necessary to ensure its stability. Dobrahas been, in the last 25 years, one of the main variables used by BancoCentral in the process of identifying a solid framework for the functioning of the economy. Thus, it was the subject of some adjustments aimed at ensuring the necessary balance between its facial value, the denominations and the evolution of the economy. Dobra's current family has been in circulation for more than two decades. This carries high risks for the country, as a result of the misadjustment of the face value of the banknotes to the economic reality and the considerable increase in cases of counterfeiting. Developments in the main macroeconomic indicators in recent years point to economic stability and nominal convergence, which are based on the adoption of exchange rate parity between the Fold and the Euro and the growth of economic activity. Today, under the above assumptions, monetary reform is necessary. In this sense, we take advantage of this commemorative date to carry out the official launch of the Monetary Reform 2018, under the motto Dobra stronger and safer, thus marking a new era of Dobra. The new fold family contains six denominations in banknotes and five in coins, observing the suppression of three zeros, without changing the purchasing power of each santomense; it includes a note of higher facial value (200 folds) to facilitate the dynamics of economic activity; it is stronger and more resilient to counterfeiting because it incorporates safety standards that are compatible with industry-defined standards; and, finally, it considers a new substrate, the polymer, for the banknotes of greater circulation with the public and subject to greater wear: those of nDb5.00 and nDb10.00. The process of this Monetary Reform will comply with all the essential criteria of a project of this great purpose, the transversality of which is undeniable. I therefore take the opportunity to invite everyone, without exception, to actively participate in this process, which contributes to the materialization of a new paradigm for the national economy. Following what I have just set out, it seems clear to me that the challenges facing BCSTP attest to the capacity and resilience of its Board of Directors and its employees in general. The prevailing picture remains one of great battles for our Institution and the search for solutions for them challenges us to be attentive to the new dynamics of the markets. S.TomeePrincipe, similar to the most diverse for ages, adopted in 2016 a Financial Sector Development Plan, which triggered a set of structural reforms of the National Financial System, with the aim of accelerating the convergence of this sector to international standards. We recognise that the successful implementation of the objectives set out in this valuable instrument will depend primarily on the commitment of all actors, direct and indirect, in the financial system and on its proper functioning. The Central Bank, today as in the past, is engaged in the consolidation of the financial system and strongly committed to putting the sector truly at the service of the national economy. To this end, we embrace a strategic agenda that combines, among others, the full and effective performance of monetary and exchange authority functions, the modernization and robustness of the financial system, literacy and financial inclusion, and communication with the outside world. In this context, we will continue with the reforms of the legal and regulatory framework and strengthen the instruments for analysing the nature of the activities pursued by the supervised institutions and improve the methods of identifying, assessing and managing the different types of risk associated with the exercise of financial activity. In our opinion, the pursuit of excellence in the standards of supervision work presupposes that the modernization process is even accelerated, aiming to strengthen the financial system with regard to risk management and resolution of banking crises. In this perspective, it is urgent to improve the instruments of monitoring of the indicators of soundness and stability of the financial system, avoiding the occurrence of events that may, in the future, affect the health of the sector, the confidenceof economic agents and, therefore, safeguardthe economy from possible losses. In the short term, we will improve the instruments for measuring the quality of the information collected together from the financial system, aiming at robust and variable public scrutiny to our performance and implement a New Credit Risk Center. We will continue with reformedpayment systemsto ensure the infra-structural conditions necessary for the modernization, diversification and expansion of the provision of financial services and products, with particular emphasis on the internationalization of the payment network. We will adopt, as soon as possible, a law establishing the protection mechanisms, both of the funds received from customers in exchange for the electronic money issued by the authorised institutions, or of other electronic financial services. With a look at internal dominance, we recognize that it is unavoidable to continue to strengthen the procedures that harmonize, among others, efficiency, competence, integrity and accountability, for collective objectives. In this context, particular importance will be given to the adoption of instruments that ensure adequate levels of operational risk management and compliance of internal processes to the standards required of modern central banks. The Central Bank is convinced of the importance of financial inclusion in improving the living conditions of the population. Thus, in compliance with the financial sector development plan, we soon conceived the elaboration of the National Financial Inclusion Strategy. We believe that the expansion of the financial sector should be based on solutions that do not jeopardise both the sustainability of institutions and the reasonableness of prices of financial products and services, taking advantage of the advantages of new information and communication technologies, which we urge financial institutions to continue in the development of their activities. We will continue to adopt policies that facilitate the Bank's relationship with the public, based on transparency, opportunity and credibility. In these terms, we will strive for an institution worthy of the public's trust, the respect of the otherentities complied with the highest standards required of today's central banks. Finally, we recognise that the success of our action lies in strengthening the link between fiscal and monetary and exchange rate policy, a fundamental requirement for the credibility and confidence of economic actors and other development partners. As MadreTerezade Calcutta said, today Santa "sometimes we feel that what we do is nothing but a drop of water in the sea. But the sea would be smaller if it lacked a drop." I believe that the work done over the twenty-five years of bcstp, by women and menwho have done their bestcomvistaaedification and strengthening of this institution, translates the importance of gout. The Central Bankwill be recommended as commitment of all.The grandeur of the task is commendable with the commitment that each, in his post, must assume for the realization of what was largely idealized. I would not like to waste this odd opportunity to thank the Government for all the availability of our activity and for the constant solidarity and support in the moments in which, within the scope of our legal powers, we are called to adopt energetic measures and visibility to control shocks and rebalance the resulting misfits. At the end, I recall a special tribute to all those who have collaborated with us and collaborated, sharing their knowledge and experience, in an exchange that seems healthy for the strengthening of our beloved institution. The administration,PeterDrucker, said,"The only thing we know about the future is that it will be different." And with this, I have the honor to present the new logo of the Central Bank of St. Thomas and Principe. Well-Be all.

Title: Balanco Economico of the year 2017
CentralBank: Central Bank of So Tom and Prncipe
text: Economic Balance Sheet 2017 On behalf of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of St. Thomas and Principe (BCSTP) and on my own, I begin by greeting all those who have given up on the work we undergo on the festive season, to listen to this 2017 annual economic balance sheet which, by tradition, is offered to us at the end of the year. I also take the opportunity to express our thanks to the financial institutions operating in the country, to the other national and foreign partners, bilateral and multilateral, whose collaboration has contributed to the fulfillment of the mission of the Central Bank of the Democratic Republic of S. Tome and Principe. Ladies, gentlemen, Recent information on the international environment reports growth in the global economy of around 3.6% in 2017, up from 3.1% in 2016. It also represents a substantial recovery of advanced economies, with particular enhancement to the economies of the Eurozone, which after several years of recession and stagnation, are beginning to show signs of consolidation of growth at positive levels. However, it should be noted that the recovery process has been asymmetric as economic growth remains very low in Latin America, the Middle East and sub-Saharan Africa commodity exporters, in particular oil. Uncertainties and risks associated with geopolitical tensions that could lead to a down-the-world revision of the medium-term economic scenario remain. On the other hand, despite positive developments, oil prices on the international market remain below expectations, which could result in a wave of systemic effects on the national economy, from the countries of our sub-region, dependent on this export raw material. Despite the modest improvement in the year-ending external environment, the national economy, which is already small and vulnerable, has not been resilient from the delayed effects of such a protracted and devastating global crisis. In fact, one of the most relevant features of the economic situation in S. Tome and Principe in 2017 is the difficulty of the country to strengthen its financing capacity in a sustained manner, which conditioned the implementation of planned public investments. According to the still provisional estimates, the economy is expected to record a growth in gross domestic product by around 4%, in line with the growth recorded in the last 2 years, and has contributed to this effect a greater dynamics of the tourism sector, combined with the activities of the construction, trade and financial sectors. As regards price stability, monetary and exchange rate policy combined with prudent fiscal policy have contributed to a controlled evolution of inflation, despite the shocks on the supply side of local products have experienced some inflationary pressure, seasonal in April and June, contributing to accumulated inflation of 6.1% until November, 5.4% observed in the same period. However, inflation is estimated to remain at single digits, at 6.5%. On the public finance side, budgetary consolidation requirements in an adverse context, characterised by poor external fundraising, conditioned budget implementation in 2017. Efforts continued to be made to maintain fiscal discipline, a condition, which, as is known, determinant for the sustainability of the fixed exchange rate regime in force. It should be noted that the conclusion of the third and fourth evaluation of the Extended Credit Facility programme signed with the IMF has been fulfilled, and all the quantitative performance criteria of the programme for June of this year have been met. In this financial year, the Central Bank maintained a prudent monetary policy orientation, having reduced the reference interest rate by 100 basis points from 10% to 9% and the rate of permanent liquidity-easing facility by 150 basis points, from 12.5% to 11% in June 2017. In addition, some liquidity management measures were implemented to improve the effectiveness of monetary policy transmission mechanisms. However, the effectiveness of monetary policy remains conditional on structural factors, the main high levels of non-performing credit and the low level of financial intermediation. Therefore, although nominal convergence, embodied in low and controlled inflation, is still a reality, there is still a weak elasticity of market interest rates in the face of the impulses of monetary policy measures. Credit to the economy increased by 3%, however, insufficient to cope with the contractionary trend of the monetary mass, which decreased by 6%. This evolution was mainly determined by the reduction of Net External Assets, around 25%, due to the weak collection of external resources with reference to november 2017. Net international reserves are around US47 million, corresponding to 3 months of import, in line with international recommendations. Imports of goods amounted to US108 million, representing an increase of around 12% compared to the same period. Imports of capital goods increased by 26.3%, suggesting a greater contribution of imports to gross fixed capital formation. For exports, they recorded a modest growth of around 3.5% in the first 11 months of the year compared to the same period a year earlier. This poor performance was due to the reduction in the volume of cocoa exports, resulting from the decrease of about 33% in the price of this commodity on the international market compared to that of a year ago. The balances of the trade balance and the current account remain structurally deficient, reflecting the constraints related to the competitiveness of the economy, and reveals that the country continues to live far above its possibilities, in a context of reduction of public development aid. This situation requires further efforts to urgently implement actions that strengthen the attractiveness of the business environment and facilitate the diversification of the economy towards increasing export capacity, with a view to gradually reducing the external dependence on our economy. The Santomense financial system has fared on several levels in recent years. However, there are still some constraints. The structure of the banking sector is also characterised by a high level of concentration. The low-income credit remains quite high, despite the downward trend, being around . of the total credit granted. The excessive exposure of the banking sector to credit risk associated with the quality of Assets have been determining factors in the vulnerability underlying the sector. In view of the challenges facing us as monetary, foreign exchange and supervisory authority, we embrace the implementation of the Strategy for the Development of the Financial Sector and the Strategy for the Reduction of Non-Parade Credit. At the same time, and in an articulated way, we adopted a strategic plan 2017-2020 that includes 5 pillars considered fundamental, namely (i) the full and effective performance of the functions of monetary and exchange rate authority; (ii) the modernisation and soundness of the financial system; (iii) the efficient organization and management of resources; (iv) literacy and financial inclusion; and (v) communication with the outside world. In the course of the materialization of these instruments, the improvement of the performance of the financial system in terms of profitability, capital adequacy and level of non-performing credit has been notorious. It should be noted that the unmatched credit stood at 24% in September 2017 compared to 28% in the same period. The liquidity ratio of the banking system was around 60%, much above the reference values (20%), suggesting that there is a large margin to be exploited in terms of financial intermediation. In this regard, it should also be emphasized that the high spreads of banks, the scarcity of bankprojects and the high level of credit risk are factors contributing to the weak performance of the financial intermediation sector. For the insurance sector, it presents indicators within the parameters considered satisfactory, of which profitability stands out. However, the sector accounts for only 3% of the total assets of the national financial system, corresponding to 1% of GDP. From this perspective, we believe that the effective implementation of compulsory motor liability insurance and the mandatory domicile of insurance are pillars for the effective leverage of insurance activity in the country. Ladies and gentlemen, At this time when we proceed to the economic balance sheet of the year about to end, it is necessary to emphasize the importance of implementing the Monetary Reform 2018, for our economy and for the Santomense society in general. Monetary Reform 2018 aims to strengthen confidence in our Fold by adapting it to the context of greater macroeconomic stability, as a propitiating factor for the business environment and investment. The introduction of the new fold family with a cut of 3 zeros requires of all of us an initial effort of appropriation and conversion, so we call for the involvement and commitment of all, living up to the motto "If it is Fold, it is Ours!". Monetary Reform 2018 is a "public good", since its provision necessarily requires state intervention and its benefit is for the general population, so its success will depend not only on the actions of the various public bodies but also on the intervention of each of us. Also on monetary reform, we would like to stress that during the co-circulation period, between 01/Jan. and 30/Jun./2018, the notes and coins of the current Dobra family can only be exchanged at the branches of banking institutions authorized to operate in our country and in the Central Bank itself. Ladies and gentlemen, The Central Bank considers that the realization of the country's development aspirations involves the creation of income opportunities that go beyond the level of subsistence, thus constituting an unavoidable premise in all the strategic orientation for the coming years, and to this end, it is essential to achieve levels of growth higher than those observed in recent years. The prevailing situation remains of great constraints for the country and the search for solutions for them challenges us to be attentive to the new market dynamics. Nevertheless, growth of around 5% is expected to be sustained, to a large extent, by Public Investments for the year 2018. In the meantime, the revitalisation of the private sector will play a key role in boosting economic activity as a stabiliser of domestic demand and a driver of exports. Monetary policy will be geared towards strengthening the nominal convergence process and the sustainability of the existing fixed exchange rate regime. We will also continue with reforms to improve the mechanisms for transmitting monetary policy on market interest rates. In the area of the financial sector, we will continue the ongoing reforms, thereby ensuring the necessary conditions for strengthening the sector's participation in economic activity and, we will strengthen the mechanisms for promoting transparency, with a view to protecting the banking customer. In this way, in addition to the duly audited financial statements, financial institutions should also publish a set of information enabling public scrutiny to act. At the end, I would like, on behalf of the Board of Directors and on behalf of the employees of the Central Bank S. Tome and Principe, to wish financial operators, economic agents and the general public Happy Holidays and a New Year full of Health and Prosperity. Welcome-Be to All and Thank You Very Much!
